verses.1: To you, O LORD, I give thanks with my whole heart; in the presence of the gods I sing your praise.
verses.2: I bow toward your holy temple and praise your name for your steadfast love and for your faithfulness, for you have exalted your name and your word above all things.
verses.3: On the day I called, you answered me; you strengthened me with strength in my soul.
verses.4: Let all the kings of the earth give thanks to you, O LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth.
verses.5: And let them sing in the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
verses.6: For the LORD is exalted, and he looks after the lowly, but the lofty he knows from afar.
verses.7: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you give me life; when the fury of my enemies rises, you stretch out your hand and deliver me by your right hand.
verses.8: The LORD will complete it for me; may the steadfast love of the LORD endure forever. May your works not be undone, O LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: The plural "kings" is used in the Hebrew, which is reflected in the English. 
- v. 6: The phrase "the lofty he knows from afar" reflects the Hebrew's contrast between the lowly and the lofty, with the LORD being aware of both.
- v. 7: The meaning of "you give me life" is inferred from the context of being delivered from trouble.
raw:
[1] To you, O LORD, I give thanks with my whole heart; in the presence of the gods I sing your praise.

[2] I bow toward your holy temple and praise your name for your steadfast love and for your faithfulness, for you have exalted your name and your word above all things.

[3] On the day I called, you answered me; you strengthened me with strength in my soul.

[4] Let all the kings of the earth give thanks to you, O LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth.

[5] And let them sing in the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.

[6] For the LORD is exalted, and he looks after the lowly, but the lofty he knows from afar.

[7] Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you give me life; when the fury of my enemies rises, you stretch out your hand and deliver me by your right hand.

[8] The LORD will complete it for me; may the steadfast love of the LORD endure forever. May your works not be undone, O LORD.

---
Notes
- v. 4: The plural "kings" is used in the Hebrew, which is reflected in the English. 
- v. 6: The phrase "the lofty he knows from afar" reflects the Hebrew's contrast between the lowly and the lofty, with the LORD being aware of both.
- v. 7: The meaning of "you give me life" is inferred from the context of being delivered from trouble.
